rule: entity.set(aspect, data) should be a no-op if any constituent trait is missing, leaving the entity unchanged and not triggering change detection.
question: What should entity.set(aspect, data) do if only some constituent traits are present? Distinguish what existing code establishes from a chosen new composite policy.
rationale: The instruction states set distributes each field to its owning constituent and triggers per-trait change detection, but does not specify behavior for partial presence. Existing setTrait requires the trait to be present (getStore would fail otherwise), so a safe composite policy is to no-op when incomplete.
